title: Sheinbaum rebuts Trump, says no migrant caravans have reached US border since January 2025
summary:
MEXICO CITY (AP) — Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said Thursday that no migrant caravans have reached the U.S. border since U.S. President Donald Trump returned to office in 2025, responding to his threat to double tariffs on Mexican goods unless Mexico stops migrants from traveling through its territory.
"Not a single migrant caravan has reached the north" since January 2025, Sheinbaum said at her daily news briefing.
Sheinbaum said a caravan of about 600 migrants traveling through the southern state of Chiapas had largely dispersed after its members were told that reaching the United States would be "very difficult."
Earlier Thursday, Trump claimed on Truth Social that the United States faced an "invasion" following midterm elections in which Democrats won control of Congress.
"MEXICO MUST STOP THEM, NOW, and if they do not do so, the Tariffs on Mexico will be IMMEDIATELY DOUBLED."

title: US reports record number of deportations and arrests in 2026
summary:
Share US reports record number of deportations and arrests in 2026 on social mediaThe United States government has reported a historic high in deportations and arrests this fiscal year, surpassing previous records.
The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) announced on Wednesday that Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) carried out 483,200 deportations and more than 491,000 immigration arrests in 2026.
The total number of deportations breaks all records in ICE’s 23-year history, including the previous record of 442,640 deportations made in 2025.
“Fiscal Year 2026 saw the highest number of ICE deportations and arrests for any year in ICE’s history.
September 2026 was the best September in ICE’s history in terms of arrests,” Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said in a statement.
